purpose: Trace-led fairness calibration of the CHAMP-2197 email inbox infrastructure task before a formal eight-attempt model gate.

evaluation.validity_policy: Only complete per-test verifier output on the stated task checksum enters the denominator. Setup failures and superseded verifier checksums are excluded.
evaluation.target_checkpoint: Approximately 2/4 Opus passes before the formal eight-attempt gate.

trace_findings: The verifier instantiated the service with a same-named repository even when Nest metadata showed that the candidate expected DatastoreService, causing cascading getByField failures.
Persistence required an instance account.save(db) path even though a repository-backed domain design was behaviorally equivalent.
Pagination required a bare array and omitted the datastore page-count method used by a valid pagination envelope implementation.
The fake datastore returned or filtered incorrect records for exact smartleadInboxId, $in, and $exists queries.
Atomic partial association required a particular exception class and exact write counts instead of rejection, unchanged state, and idempotent final state.
The suite prescribed entity file placement and an undocumented id alias even though the ticket names smartleadInboxId as the key.
Mapped deliverability was tied to one property name and the prompt did not clearly distinguish the numeric reputation from its band.
The persistence test omitted the Smartlead response required by a valid entity-level hydration design.
fairness_changes: Clarified numeric reputation versus mapped deliverability band, duplicate inbox IDs, and atomic rejection in the prompt.
Selected the service dependency from emitted Nest constructor metadata.
Accepted service-, repository-, or entity-level persistence and flexible entity module placement.
Made pagination, identity, deliverability-band aliases, and association assertions behavior-based.
Implemented faithful exact, $in, $exists, pagination, page-count, and Smartlead HTTP mocks.
requirements_preserved: Smartlead identity, client, email, domain, tags, campaign IDs, and derived campaign count
numeric warm-up reputation plus mapped High, Medium, Low, Burned, or Unknown band
dedicated datastore persistence, ID/email/client lookup, pagination, and deletion
idempotent association and all-or-nothing rejection for missing inbox IDs
four-factor ranking and floor-based campaign pool sizing
Smartlead creation-time and reputation hydration with explicit not-found behavior
controller, module, operational scripts, and existing regression behavior

excluded_diagnostic_waves.reason: Superseded after traces showed incorrect constructor dependency injection and remaining mock/alias coupling.
Superseded because one valid entity placement failed suite loading and one 11/12 implementation used an omitted datastore getPageCount method.

Superseded because two correct smartleadInboxId-only designs were still read through an undocumented id alias and entity-level persistence lacked a hydration HTTP stub. One zero-cost NVM network failure was excluded.

failed_attempt_findings: Did not persist the mapped deliverability band despite exposing it on the in-memory domain object.
Crashed while rehydrating persisted records because Object.assign attempted to write the campaign count into a getter-only property.

excluded_infrastructure_attempt.reason: NVM download connection reset before the agent ran; two setup attempts produced no verifier outcome.

current_checkpoint.conclusion: The task is now fair and still long-horizon, but 3/4 is above the intended Opus checkpoint. Do not reintroduce architecture-specific verifier coupling; add historically supported integration or migration complexity before the formal eight-attempt gate.

next_step: Use CHAMP-2197 or adjacent ClickUp and PR evidence to add a coupled, production-backed integration or migration behavior, rerun null and oracle controls, then repeat four Opus attempts. Freeze that checksum only if the checkpoint is near 2/4 before running eight attempts each for Opus, Grok 4.5, and GPT-5.6 Sol.
